# Release rule: lentil soup 500 ml (item 2210)

Checked every Sunday after the ERP forecast run (18:00), on the last 13 valid weeks
(sold-out weeks and weeks without a stored forecast do not count).

The order quantity goes into planning without sign-off when all four check lights are green:

1. **Data:** last week's actual and this week's forecast are both available.
2. **Baseline:** the forecast's mean error is smaller than that of "same as last week".
3. **Bias:** sum (forecast − actual) is at most 5 % of sum actual, too high or too low.
4. **Range:** the actual landed inside the 80 % range at least 9 times out of 13.

Order quantity = forecast + the 79th percentile of the last 26 errors (actual − forecast).
Share 0.79 = shortage €1.50 ÷ (shortage €1.50 + leftover €0.40), from costs.md.
If the staff canteen stops collecting, the leftover cost becomes €1.60 and the share 0.48.

Otherwise **[name: who decides]** decides, and writes the quantity and the reason in the log.

Always a person, whatever the lights say: new product, a customer joins or leaves
(e.g. the organic chain delisting, April 2025), price change of more than 10 %,
supply shortage, promotion not yet in the ERP promotion calendar.

final_text:
Yes, the forecast is usable. Cook **748 jars** for the week of 29 December. One caveat: it's New Year's week, and the forecast for this same week last year came out too high.

The 94.2% figure is real (the ERP calculates it as 1 minus the error rate, 5.8%), but it leaves out two things. It doesn't compare the tool against a simple rule, and it doesn't show which direction the misses go. The tool's forecasts lean slightly high, and earlier this year it went off track for three months after you lost a customer.

**What I checked:** 30 Dec 2024 to 22 Dec 2025, 50 weeks. Two weeks are left out: 3 Feb 2025 (no forecast stored because of the ERP update) and 10 Mar 2025 (sold out, so sales were below demand). The week of 16 Sep 2024 appears twice in the file, so I counted it once.

| | Average miss (jars) | Bias | Error rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| ERP forecast | 33.3 | 3.0 % too high | 5.8 % |
| "Same as last week" | 42.2 | 0.3 % too low | 7.4 % |

1. **Against a simple rule:** the forecast misses by 21% less than "cook the same as last week", and it was closer in 30 of 50 weeks. The best simple rule would have been "same as the same week last year" (average miss of 38.8 jars). The forecast beats that too.
2. **Forecast range:** in 36 of 50 weeks, actual sales fell inside the range covering 80% of past misses. The misses that fell outside are concentrated from April 2025 onward. They start after the note for 7 April: "Organic market chain with 9 stores delists the lentil soup (about 70 jars a week)."
3. **How many to cook for 29 Dec 2025:** the forecast is 729 jars, and the likely range is 694 to 756.
   - Your costs are €1.50 for a missing jar and €0.40 for a leftover. That makes running short almost four times as costly as a leftover, so cooking at a level that is enough about 79% of the time gives **748 jars**.
   - 748 would have been too few in 5 of the last 26 weeks.
   - Over the past year, cooking this way would have cost about €1,023 in shortages and leftovers. Cooking exactly the forecast would have cost €1,105, and "same as last week" €2,052.
4. **Release rule:** all four checks are green, so 748 can go into planning without anyone signing off.
   - **Red weeks in the last year:** 15 of 52. That's 3 Feb 2025 (no forecast stored) and every week from 21 Apr to 21 Jul 2025, when the forecast ran too high and too many weeks fell outside the range. It kept forecasting the old volume for about three months after the delisting.

Things worth checking:
- **New Year's week:** last year the forecast for this week was 703 and you sold 678. This year it forecasts 729, almost the same as last week's 733 sales. If you expect a holiday dip again, whoever decides should judge that. With the costs as they are, being short still costs more than having jars left over.
- **The canteen:** 748 assumes it keeps collecting leftovers at €1.20 a jar. If it doesn't, a leftover costs €1.60 and the number to cook drops noticeably.

I wrote the release rule to `pruefregel-lentil-soup.md`. It needs one name from you: who decides in weeks when a check is red. It also says a person should always decide when a customer joins or leaves, so the next delisting gets handled by someone rather than by the tool.

follow_ups.final_text:
Cook **729 jars**, which is exactly what the ERP forecasts. That's 19 fewer than the 748 from before.

**Why it drops:** a leftover jar now costs the full €1.60 to make. That's slightly more than the €1.50 you lose on a missing jar, so the extra jars you cooked as a buffer against running short are no longer worth it. The best level is now a quantity that's enough about half the time (48%), not 79% as before. With this forecast's past misses, that lands exactly on the forecast.

| | Before (canteen pays €1.20) | Now (no canteen) |
|---|---|---|
| Leftover jar costs | €0.40 | €1.60 |
| Share of weeks it should be enough | 79 % | 48 % |
| **Jars to cook** | **748** | **729** |
| Weeks out of the last 26 it would have been too few | 5 | 13 |

- **Range for the week:** still 694 to 756 jars.
- **Checks:** all four are still green, so 729 can go into planning without sign-off.
- **Cost over the past year:** if leftovers had cost €1.60 all year, cooking this way would have cost about €2,497 in shortages and leftovers. Cooking exactly the forecast would have cost €2,621, and "same as last week" €3,270. The same quantity costs more overall now because every leftover jar is a full loss.

The holiday point from before still applies. Last year the forecast for this week was 25 jars too high. Now that leftovers cost more than shortages, that matters more. If you expect a dip around New Year, whoever decides can go below 729, but they should log the reason.

Also, if you find another buyer for leftovers, even at a low price, the number to cook goes back up. It would also go up if you count an empty shelf as costing you something with the shops; `costs.md` says to add that to the shortage cost and write down why.

I updated `pruefregel-lentil-soup.md` with the new costs. It still needs the name of the person who decides when a check is red.
